question: Roughly what percentage of surface contaminants can be removed just by taking off a victim's outer clothes?

options.A: About 80 percent
options.B: Exactly 50 percent
options.C: Only 5 percent
options.D: Nearly 100 percent

explanation: Fascinating fact! Simply stripping off contaminated outer clothing gets rid of the vast majority of harmful chemicals right away.

question: Why is community participation a core requirement for mental health promotion?

options.A: It prevents nurses from having to visit villages
options.B: It stops people from asking questions about their treatment
options.C: It saves the government from spending any money on health
options.D: It ensures programs fit local realities and gain genuine acceptance

explanation: When local people help design programs, the solutions match their actual cultural needs and people are much more likely to use them. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T7#GNS314_U4_T7_h2)

question: Which property of the skin allows patches and creams to deliver medication into the body?

options.A: High concentration of sweat and oil glands
options.B: Continuous shedding of the outer epidermis
options.C: Semi-permeability to lipid-soluble substances
options.D: Thick layer of insulating subcutaneous fat

explanation: Certain medications can pass through the skin barrier because the skin is semi-permeable to fat-soluble compounds. [learn more](GNS211_U2_T5#GNS211_U2_T5_h7)

question: What is the best way for a nurse to teach a client how to use a condom properly?

options.A: Ask them to watch a video without asking questions
options.B: Demonstrate the technique using a model and let the client practice
options.C: Hand them a printed pamphlet to read at home
options.D: Explain the chemical composition of latex in detail

explanation: You're right! Showing them on a model and having them try it builds real confidence and ensures they get the steps right.

question: Why can steroid hormones slip right out of cells as soon as they are made?

options.A: They are pushed out by water pressure inside the cytoplasm
options.B: They are small enough to pass through active transport protein pumps
options.C: They are stored in large vesicles that burst open upon stimulation
options.D: They are fat-soluble and can cross lipid cell membranes easily

explanation: Because cell membranes are also made of fats (lipids), fat-loving steroid hormones pass straight through them like an open door—no special channels needed!

question: What is the most important factor when checking if a patient is ready for a high-tech mobility device?

options.A: The current market price of the technology
options.B: The brand name of the device manufacturer
options.C: The patient's cognitive status and judgment
options.D: The color preference of the patient's family

explanation: You got it! A patient's thinking ability and good judgment are key to making sure they can use high-tech gear safely.

question: Which organ needs routine blood test monitoring when a patient is on long-term azole antifungal therapy?

options.A: Thyroid
options.B: Heart
options.C: Lungs
options.D: Liver

explanation: Azole drugs are processed by the liver, so we keep an eye on liver enzymes during long-term therapy to catch any stress early.

question: What is the medical term for the complete absence of menstrual periods?

options.A: Menorrhagia
options.B: Dysmenorrhea
options.C: Amenorrhea
options.D: Metrorrhagia

explanation: Amenorrhea simply means 'no menses.' It can be primary (if periods never started) or secondary (if regular periods stopped).

question: You just finished dressing a patient's wound with blood-stained gauze. Which bin should this gauze go into?

options.A: Black bin
options.B: Brown bin
options.C: Yellow bin
options.D: Clear bin

explanation: Well done! Blood-soaked materials are considered infectious waste, so they always go into the yellow bin or bag for safe, specialized treatment.

question: Which type of parasitic egg is known for having a little lid (operculum) or a sharp spine?

options.A: Trematode ova
options.B: Nematode ova
options.C: Bacterial spores
options.D: Cestode ova

explanation: Flukes, or trematodes, lay eggs with a tiny lid or spine to help the larva escape. Spot on!

question: Why is the chain of infection like a link fence? What happens if you break just one link?

options.A: Pathogens require all six links to survive inside a reservoir
options.B: Breaking any single link stops the infection from spreading
options.C: The immune system only attacks pathogens when all links are full
options.D: Microorganisms multiply faster when every link is connected

explanation: You've got it! Think of infection control as stopping a chain reaction. If you wash your hands or clean a surface, you break the chain of transmission and stop the disease in its tracks.

question: What happens to a patient's red blood cells if they are given a severely hypotonic intravenous solution?

options.A: They remain completely unchanged
options.B: They immediately multiply rapidly
options.C: They swell and may burst
options.D: They shrink and shrivel up

explanation: In a hypotonic solution, water rushes into the cells because the surrounding fluid has a lower solute concentration, causing the cells to swell and potentially rupture (lysis). [learn more](GNS111_U1_T5#GNS111_U1_T5_h6)

question: What three main disciplines are combined in nursing informatics?

options.A: Biology, pharmacology, and hospital administration
options.B: Nursing science, computer science, and information science
options.C: Public health, statistics, and clinical psychology
options.D: Medicine, engineering, and health economics

explanation: Nursing informatics is defined by the integration of nursing science with computer and information sciences to manage healthcare data. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T2#GNS113_U2_T2_h1)

question: What do we call passing an STI from a mother to her baby during childbirth?

options.A: Fomite transfer
options.B: Vertical transmission
options.C: Horizontal transmission
options.D: Systemic inoculation

explanation: Vertical transmission simply means passing an infection from mother to child during pregnancy, labor, or delivery. You've got this!

question: What does it mean when a microorganism is simply 'colonizing' a patient?

options.A: The microorganism lives on or in the body without causing tissue damage
options.B: The pathogen has invaded deep tissues and caused severe organ failure
options.C: The bacteria are spreading rapidly through the bloodstream to the brain
options.D: The immune system has completely destroyed all traces of the microbe

explanation: Colonization means the germ is hanging out and multiplying on the skin or mucous membranes without making the person actively sick.

question: Which learning disability specifically impairs a person's ability to perform mathematical calculations?

options.A: Apraxia
options.B: Dysgraphia
options.C: Dyslexia
options.D: Dyscalculia

explanation: Dyscalculia is the specific neurological term for difficulties involving numbers and math concepts. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T6#GNS324_U4_T6_h2)

question: What is tele-nursing mainly all about?

options.A: The training of nursing students through online video lectures
options.B: A computerized machine that automatically administers medications
options.C: An online filing system used strictly for hospital record keeping
options.D: The practice of nursing care delivered over a distance using technology

explanation: You got this! Tele-nursing simply means using phones, video calls, or apps to connect with patients remotely, giving them guidance and support without needing to be right beside them.

question: What is needed to make sure digital gadgets and tech actually help student learning?

options.A: Good teacher training and reliable school infrastructure
options.B: Making students wear VR headsets for every single class
options.C: Throwing away all printed nursing textbooks
options.D: Restricting computer use only to top school admin staff

explanation: Tech is only helpful if your school has steady power, working equipment, and teachers who know how to use it with you.

question: Why might two people taking the exact same dose of cough syrup react completely differently?

options.A: The color of the syrup changes how fast the stomach digests it.
options.B: Different brands use completely different active ingredients.
options.C: The time of day changes the weight of the medication.
options.D: Genetic differences in liver enzymes affect drug breakdown rates.

explanation: We all process drugs at our own pace because of our unique liver enzymes (like CYP2D6)! One person might clear it fast, while another feels it much longer.

question: What shape is an intrauterine device (IUD)?

options.A: T-shaped
options.B: Spiral-shaped
options.C: Capsule-shaped
options.D: Ring-shaped

explanation: IUDs are built with a small frame shaped like the letter T so they fit comfortably inside the uterine cavity. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T015#GNS226_U6_T015_h1)

question: What is a major job of international groups like the FAO in the food chain?

options.A: Directly managing hospital nutrition wards during health crises
options.B: Owning and operating all commercial farms in developing nations
options.C: Monitoring global agricultural production and issuing early famine warnings
options.D: Setting retail prices for grocery stores in local communities

explanation: Organizations like the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) keep an eye on crop conditions worldwide so they can warn countries before a famine hits.

question: Which of the following is NOT an ethical practice when presenting qualitative research results?

options.A: Revealing the real names of participants to give them credit
options.B: Reporting all findings honestly, even unexpected ones
options.C: Separating factual results from personal opinions
options.D: Using pseudonyms to protect participant confidentiality

explanation: Participant confidentiality is paramount; revealing real names without explicit consent breaches ethical research standards. [learn more](GNS224_U2_T4#GNS224_U2_T4_h6)

question: Why do state or regional health schemes often exist alongside a national scheme?

options.A: To address local health priorities and specific regional demographics
options.B: To compete directly with private international clinics
options.C: To prevent rural residents from visiting city hospitals
options.D: To collect extra taxes without government approval

explanation: Correct! State schemes let local governments customize health packages to fit the unique cultural and financial needs of their own people.

question: Why is it so important for nurses to check in on a patient's mental health during post-abortion care?

options.A: Patients with mental distress are legally barred from receiving contraceptives
options.B: Psychological symptoms interfere directly with the absorption of oral antibiotics
options.C: Hospital insurance policies refuse to pay claims without a mental health diagnosis
options.D: Physical healing alone does not address hidden trauma, anxiety, and depression

explanation: Treating the physical body is only half the job. The secrecy and stress surrounding unsafe abortions leave deep emotional wounds that also need healing and gentle support.

question: Which medication is routinely given right after baby is born to prevent heavy bleeding?

options.A: Magnesium sulfate
options.B: Paracetamol
options.C: Insulin
options.D: Oxytocin

explanation: Oxytocin is our best friend in the third stage of labor! It makes the uterus clamp down tight, squeezing off blood vessels to keep bleeding under control.

question: Why do nurses need to monitor organ function regularly in patients with systemic autoimmune conditions?

options.A: It prevents patients from developing contagious bacterial infections
options.B: It eliminates the need for any future blood tests
options.C: Widespread inflammation can silently damage vital organs like the kidneys and heart
options.D: It proves whether the patient is following their prescribed diet

explanation: Systemic flare-ups don't just hurt joints—they can quietly cause internal damage over time, making routine checkups a lifesaver.

question: What type of health issue usually spikes during the first few hours of a sudden disaster?

options.A: Delayed seasonal allergy symptoms
options.B: Acute physical trauma and injuries
options.C: Chronic degenerative nerve disorders
options.D: Long-term nutritional deficiencies

explanation: Right after sudden events like storms or earthquakes, the most common sights are physical injuries, cuts, and fractures that need immediate care.

question: Who is expected to show leadership skills in a healthcare setting?

options.A: Only senior physicians and surgical consultants
options.B: Only the director of nursing and hospital chief executive
options.C: Administrative staff who manage patient records
options.D: Every nurse, regardless of formal administrative rank

explanation: You don't need a fancy title to be a leader! Every nurse shows leadership when coordinating bedside care or supporting teammates.

question: What is the primary goal of a Root Cause Analysis (RCA) after a major incident?

options.A: To fulfill government tax requirements for medical centers
options.B: To find out which specific nurse or doctor should be fired
options.C: To calculate total financial damages owed to the patient's family
options.D: To uncover deep underlying system flaws that allowed the error

explanation: Spot on! RCA digs past surface mistakes to find the environmental and procedural triggers that caused the event.

question: An infant receives protective antibodies through breast milk. What type of immunity is this?

options.A: Natural active immunity
options.B: Artificial passive immunity
options.C: Artificial active immunity
options.D: Natural passive immunity

explanation: This is natural passive immunity because the mother's antibodies pass naturally to the baby to give temporary protection.

question: Why should nurses take parents seriously when they worry about their toddler's social development?

options.A: Doctors require parental permission to perform physical exams
options.B: Family concerns are more accurate than formal medical tests
options.C: Parents usually exaggerate normal childhood naughtiness
options.D: Caregivers are often the first to notice early developmental differences

explanation: Parents spend the most time with their little ones and usually spot early warning signs before anyone else walks into the room. Trust their insights!

question: Which common side effect often occurs due to the stimulant properties of bronchodilators like albuterol?

options.A: Rapid heart rate and palpitations
options.B: Uncontrollable drowsiness and sleep
options.C: Severe drop in blood pressure
options.D: Complete loss of the sense of taste

explanation: Beta-agonist bronchodilators stimulate heart receptors, frequently causing a fast heartbeat or jittery feeling. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T7#GNS212_U2_T7_h7)

question: Why is teaching patients how to read food labels so important on a low-fat diet?

options.A: Processed foods often contain hidden fats that are not obvious by appearance.
options.B: Labels help the patient calculate the exact cost of groceries.
options.C: Reading labels is a legal requirement for hospital discharge.
options.D: Nutrition labels tell the patient exactly when to take their medications.

explanation: Many packaged snacks hide extra fats where you least expect them. Reading labels helps patients spot those sneaky lipids!

question: A Nigerian dietitian is counseling a patient with high blood pressure who has a modest income. What is the most practical advice?

options.A: Recommend affordable local foods and suggest low-salt preparation methods
options.B: Tell the patient to rely entirely on hospital meal deliveries
options.C: Advise the patient to stop eating all local carbohydrates completely
options.D: Prescribe expensive imported supplements available only online

explanation: Spot on! Good counseling must fit the patient's pocket. It's always best to recommend healthy, accessible local foods prepared with less salt.

question: Why do nurses track balancing measures during an improvement project?

options.A: To detect any unintended negative consequences in other parts of the system
options.B: To compare the hospital performance against international standards
options.C: To balance the nursing unit's monthly financial budget and payroll
options.D: To ensure that doctors and nurses work the exact same number of hours

explanation: Brilliant! Balancing measures act like an early warning system to make sure fixing one problem doesn't accidentally cause another one somewhere else.

question: Why does the anterior pituitary gland enlarge during normal pregnancy?

options.A: Enlargement due to retained fluid volume
options.B: Proliferation of prolactin-secreting cells
options.C: Hypertrophy of cells producing growth hormone
options.D: Increased storage of oxytocin for delivery

explanation: The anterior pituitary grows noticeably larger because the cells that produce prolactin multiply rapidly to prepare the mother's body for breastfeeding. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T7#GNS121_U7_T7_h2)

question: What is the main goal of creating a "Just Culture" in a hospital?

options.A: To eliminate all forms of nursing accountability for clinical mistakes
options.B: To ensure that every person who makes a mistake is fired immediately
options.C: To protect the hospital administration from medical malpractice lawsuits
options.D: To encourage honest reporting of errors without the immediate fear of punishment

explanation: Brilliant! A Just Culture means we can speak up honestly when things go wrong without shaking in our boots, so the whole team can learn and fix the system.

question: What happens at the end of a Build-Operate-Transfer (BOT) arrangement?

options.A: The private company permanently owns the hospital building
options.B: The management contract is automatically renewed forever
options.C: The facility is demolished to build commercial real estate
options.D: Ownership of the facility is transferred back to the government

explanation: As the name says, 'BOT' means the private partner builds and runs it for a set time, then hands the keys back to the government!

question: Why is a Venturi mask often chosen for patients with COPD?

options.A: It pumps high-pressure air directly into the stomach.
options.B: It allows the patient to eat and drink without removing it.
options.C: It delivers a precise and controlled concentration of oxygen.
options.D: It completely eliminates the need for any humidification.

explanation: Venturi masks use clever color-coded adapters to give an exact percentage of oxygen, keeping vulnerable COPD patients safe.

question: Why are regular simulation drills so helpful for disaster response teams?

options.A: They replace the need for community education and public awareness campaigns
options.B: They generate immediate revenue from ticket sales to spectators
options.C: They ensure that national politicians take personal charge of rescue work
options.D: They test equipment readiness and improve coordination among different responding agencies

explanation: Spot on! Practice makes perfect. Simulations let teams test their gear and teamwork *before* a real emergency catches them off guard.

question: Which of these is part of the external male reproductive system?

options.A: Seminal vesicle
options.B: Prostate gland
options.C: Vas deferens
options.D: Scrotum

explanation: The scrotum and the penis are on the outside (external), while the prostate, vas deferens, and seminal vesicles are tucked inside the body.

question: Which healthcare approach works best when teaching young people about reproductive health?

options.A: Mandatory public announcements broadcast only in corporate workplaces
options.B: Strict punitive laws targeting teenagers seeking health information
options.C: Youth-friendly clinics offering confidential counseling and contraceptives
options.D: Excluding adolescents from family planning discussions until marriage

explanation: Young people want privacy and a welcoming environment without fear of being scolded. Youth-friendly clinics build trust so teens actually feel safe seeking help!

question: What is a very common challenge for clients after prostate surgery?

options.A: Permanent loss of the ability to digest proteins
options.B: Chronic infections of the upper respiratory tract
options.C: Urinary incontinence and erectile dysfunction
options.D: Sudden enlargement of the thyroid gland in the neck

explanation: Because the prostate sits right next to the nerves and muscles controlling urination and erections, surgery here often causes temporary or lasting trouble with both functions.

question: Which agricultural expense involves paying planting crews and harvesting staff?

options.A: Seed patents
options.B: Fertilizer tariffs
options.C: Labor costs
options.D: Environmental subsidies

explanation: Labor encompasses the wages paid to workers who physically plant, manage, and harvest crops. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T026#GNS227_U2_T026_h2)

question: What is a reservoir in the chain of infection?

options.A: The method used by a microbe to travel to a new host
options.B: The natural habitat where a pathogen lives and multiplies
options.C: The specific entry point through broken skin
options.D: A person who has complete immunity against disease

explanation: A reservoir acts as the home base where germs live, grow, and reproduce before moving to a new host. [learn more](GST114_U1_T3#GST114_U1_T3_h2)

question: What is the primary job of the Leydig cells found in the testes?

options.A: To store mature sperm cells
options.B: To produce alkaline seminal fluid
options.C: To secrete testosterone
options.D: To nourish the urinary bladder

explanation: Leydig cells live right between the sperm-producing tubes and act as the main factories for pumping out testosterone in the male body.

question: Why shouldn't a nurse just do everything for a slow patient who can manage with a tool?

options.A: To save nursing time for charting and other patients
options.B: To ensure the patient finishes dressing before visiting hours
options.C: To foster independence and prevent learned helplessness
options.D: Because hospital policy strictly forbids nurse assistance

explanation: Brilliant! We want to cheer them on to do it themselves so they don't become overly dependent on us.

question: How does social justice guide a community health nurse during advocacy?

options.A: It drives the nurse to fight for fair access to health resources for everyone
options.B: It requires the nurse to obey hospital management without question
options.C: It forces the nurse to prioritize wealthy patients who pay higher taxes
options.D: It allows the nurse to make medical diagnoses independently

explanation: Well done! Social justice is about fairness—making sure everyone, rich or poor, gets a fair share of healthcare resources to close health gaps.

question: What happens during systemic absorption of a topical medication?

options.A: The drug evaporates into the air without touching living skin cells
options.B: The drug enters dermal blood vessels and travels to distant organs
options.C: The drug stays strictly on the outer surface of the epidermis
options.D: The drug remains completely trapped inside the stratum corneum layer

explanation: Systemic action happens when the drug penetrates deep enough to hit the blood capillaries in the dermis, allowing the bloodstream to carry it throughout the body. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T16#GNS125_U3_T16_h4)

question: Which of these is NOT an accessory organ of digestion?

options.A: The gallbladder
options.B: The pancreas
options.C: The stomach
options.D: The liver

explanation: Food actually passes right through the stomach as part of the main tube (alimentary canal). The liver, pancreas, and gallbladder sit off to the side as trusty helpers, making them accessory organs!

question: Why does the intestinal wall have a muscular layer (the muscularis)?

options.A: Secreting hormones into the bloodstream
options.B: Generating peristaltic waves to move contents
options.C: Filtering waste from local blood vessels
options.D: Absorbing digested sugars and amino acids

explanation: These muscles squeeze in a coordinated wave pattern (peristalsis) to push food smoothly along the digestive tract. You've got this!

question: What is a major plus of using comfort measures (like heat or rest) alongside medicines?

options.A: They guarantee the patient will have zero bleeding
options.B: They help reduce the overall need for heavy pain medications
options.C: They completely eliminate the need for any vital sign checks
options.D: They cure underlying infections without antibiotics

explanation: Combining simple comfort tricks with meds gives wonderful relief while keeping heavy drug use to a minimum. You're thinking like a holistic nurse!

question: Why is complete chest recoil important between compressions?

options.A: It keeps the electrical conduction system stable
options.B: It gives the rescuer a chance to rest their arms
options.C: It allows the heart chambers to refill with blood
options.D: It prevents broken ribs in older adults

explanation: Without full chest recoil, the heart stays partly squeezed and cannot fill properly for the next push. [learn more](GNS315_U4_T4#GNS315_U4_T4_h2)

question: What is the proper way to dispose of expired cytotoxic drugs?

options.A: Send them for specialized high-temperature incineration
options.B: Treat them in a low-heat autoclave
options.C: Pour them down the clinical sink with plenty of water
options.D: Bury them in a normal municipal landfill

explanation: Cytotoxic drugs have tough chemical structures, so they need intense, high-temperature incineration to be safely destroyed.

question: Which of the following is a common positive result of using person-centered care?

options.A: Decreased staffing requirements across all shifts
options.B: Shorter hospital stays for acute trauma patients
options.C: Reduced behavioral symptoms in residents with dementia
options.D: Elimination of the need for any medication administration

explanation: Spot on! When patients feel heard, respected, and comfortable, it often lowers anxiety and reduces challenging behaviors in dementia.

question: Why is staff health considered a key component of the School Health Programme?

options.A: Staff members consume the majority of school meals
options.B: Adults are more prone to infections than young children
options.C: Teachers are legally required to work twenty-four hours daily
options.D: Healthy staff serve as role models and maintain productivity

explanation: Staff well-being directly impacts the quality of teaching and ensures that adults model healthy behaviors for students. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T3#GNS225_U4_T3_h6)

question: What is one of the most common causes of medication errors on a busy hospital ward?

options.A: Distractions and interruptions during preparation
options.B: Writing patient names clearly in black ink
options.C: Performing three checks against the prescription order
options.D: Asking patients to state their date of birth

explanation: Noise and interruptions break your focus. When drawing up meds or checking doses, try to find a quiet zone to avoid silly mistakes!

question: Why is gripping small mobile tablets with just one hand for a long time risky for nurses?

options.A: It can cause repetitive strain injuries in the fingers and thumbs
options.B: It reduces the wireless signal strength of the device
options.C: It permanently ruins the electronic screen display calibration
options.D: It causes immediate bone fractures in the wrist bones

explanation: Correct! Small, repeated hand movements without a break can easily irritate your tendons and nerves. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T3#GNS113_U3_T3_h5)

question: How can you best describe the latent stage of conflict?

options.A: The disagreement is fully resolved and teamwork is restored.
options.B: Individuals realize a problem exists without feeling any emotion.
options.C: Conditions exist for friction, but no dispute has happened yet.
options.D: Staff members are actively yelling at each other in the hallway.

explanation: In the latent stage, the ingredients for a fight are quietly sitting there in the background, but nobody has actually clashed yet. It's the calm before the potential storm.

question: Which sociological theory suggests that older adults remain happier and healthier when they stay busy and socially involved?

options.A: Free radical theory
options.B: Activity theory
options.C: Disengagement theory
options.D: Wear-and-tear theory

explanation: Activity theory proposes that staying socially active and maintaining roles promotes well-being in older age. [learn more](GNS321_U3_T1#GNS321_U3_T1_h3)

question: What is the most important rule when picking a theoretical framework for your study?

options.A: It must be a grand theory rather than a middle-range theory
options.B: It must be approved by the hospital nursing director
options.C: It must naturally match the specific research problem and variables
options.D: It must be the most recently published theory in nursing literature

explanation: Right! Your framework has to make logical sense with what you are trying to find out. Never force a mismatch.

question: Why does a low count of CD4+ T cells make a person vulnerable to many different infections?

options.A: CD4+ cells act as master coordinators that signal other immune cells to fight germs.
options.B: CD4+ cells are responsible for carrying oxygen to fighting white cells.
options.C: CD4+ cells physically trap and digest bacteria in the bloodstream.
options.D: CD4+ cells produce thick mucus barriers on skin and mucous membranes.

explanation: Think of CD4+ cells as the generals in an army. Without them giving orders, the rest of the immune defenses don't know when or how to attack germs!

question: Which complication of long bone fractures (like the femur) involves breathing trouble and a spotty rash?

options.A: Fat embolism syndrome
options.B: Osteomyelitis infection
options.C: Superficial skin breakdown
options.D: Chronic bone spur formation

explanation: Fat droplets from inside the bone marrow can slip into the bloodstream after a long bone break, traveling to the lungs and brain. Watch out for breathing issues and a petechial rash!

question: Which disease category needs to be reported immediately within 24 hours because it can spark a fast epidemic?

options.A: Category 3
options.B: Category 1
options.C: Category 2
options.D: Category 4

explanation: Spot on! Category 1 diseases are serious emergencies that require instant notification—sometimes with a quick phone call right away.

question: Which factor most frequently disrupts healthy eating habits during adolescence?

options.A: An inability to digest complex carbohydrates
options.B: Peer pressure and preoccupation with body image
options.C: A natural biological loss of interest in eating
options.D: The complete disappearance of hunger cues

explanation: Teens care a lot about fitting in and body image. Peer pressure and media trends often push them toward skipping meals or strict dieting.

question: A clinic finds 20 people with malaria in a town of 4,000 residents. What is the prevalence per 1,000 people?
explanation: Divide 20 by 4,000 to get 0.005, then multiply by 1,000 to get 5 per 1,000 people. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T12#GNS313_U1_T12_h3)

question: How do grief and mourning differ from each other?

options.A: Grief is a medical diagnosis, while mourning is a nursing intervention
options.B: Grief only happens in hospitals, while mourning happens at home
options.C: Grief is the internal emotional feeling, while mourning is the outward expression
options.D: Grief lasts for years, while mourning ends after a few days

explanation: Think of grief as what happens inside your heart and mind, while mourning is how you show it on the outside through cultural or religious practices.

question: Which of these conditions is best suited for ongoing tele-nursing management?

options.A: Acute traumatic limb amputation
options.B: Emergency cardiac arrest
options.C: Hypertension and diabetes
options.D: Sudden severe appendicitis

explanation: Correct! Chronic illnesses that need daily lifestyle support and regular checks are perfect candidates for virtual follow-ups.

question: What is the main purpose of the HEEADSSS tool when assessing a teenager?

options.A: To systematically screen for lifestyle risk factors and psychosocial health
options.B: To diagnose underlying genetic disorders of the endocrine system
options.C: To calculate the exact caloric requirements for daily exercise
options.D: To determine the precise biological stage of puberty

explanation: Spot on! HEEADSSS is a helpful checklist nurses use to review a teen's home life, school, mental health, and safety.

question: A nurse teaches mothers why immunization prevents killer childhood diseases. Which learning domain is this mainly addressing?

options.A: Cognitive domain
options.B: Affective domain
options.C: Psychomotor domain
options.D: Financial domain

explanation: Teaching the reasons behind disease prevention and building mental understanding targets the cognitive domain of knowledge.

question: How should a nurse handle personal religious beliefs when faced with an emergency PAC case?

options.A: By prioritizing the immediate life-saving care and treating the client without judgment
options.B: By transferring the patient to another facility without stabilization
options.C: By lecturing the client on morality before administering intravenous fluids
options.D: By refusing to touch the patient until a religious leader speaks with her

explanation: In an emergency, saving a patient's life and providing compassionate nursing care always comes before personal opinions.

question: Why do we choose the intradermal route instead of subcutaneous for allergy skin tests?

options.A: It allows safe observation of a localized skin response
options.B: It triggers a rapid whole-body immune reaction
options.C: It is completely painless for the patient
options.D: It delivers a larger volume of testing solution

explanation: Great job! Intradermal injections let us easily watch how the skin reacts locally to allergens or TB tests without spreading the solution all over the body.

question: What is the main reason nurses perform a nutritional assessment on a patient?

options.A: To calculate the exact cost of the patient's hospital meals
options.B: To prescribe specific dietary supplements right away
options.C: To diagnose rare genetic disorders affecting metabolism

question: What is a top nursing priority right after a reproductive surgery like a hysterectomy?

options.A: Restricting all fluid intake for the first 48 hours

options.D: Discharging the patient immediately to free up hospital beds

question: What is the main reason a patient must stay NPO (nothing by mouth) before surgery?

options.A: To reduce the cost of hospital meals
options.B: To speed up post-operative wound healing
options.C: To prevent sudden spikes in blood pressure
options.D: To prevent aspiration during anesthesia

question: A patient asks which eating pattern is best for keeping their blood pressure in check. What should you tell them?

options.A: A high-protein, zero-fiber carnivore diet to preserve muscle mass

options.C: A strict low-carbohydrate ketogenic diet with high saturated fats
options.D: The DASH diet rich in fruits, vegetables, and low-fat dairy

question: When is a retrospective nursing audit done?

question: What happens to the tiny coronary blood vessels when local waste products like adenosine pile up?

question: A nurse wants to find the best evidence for managing pressure ulcers before updating the ward policy. What is the most appropriate first step?

question: What is the main reason for involving community and religious leaders in youth health programs?

question: How does home care primarily change the way healthcare is delivered?

options.A: From hospital-centered interventions to daily life

question: In which direction should you smooth a topical lotion onto a patient's skin?

question: How do sebum (skin oil) and sweat team up to protect your body?

options.C: They create a thick physical padding against heavy bumps.

question: A nurse wants to help secondary school girls prevent anemia using local foods. Which tip is the most practical?

options.B: Eat sugary snacks between classes for quick energy

question: A newborn is born limp, pale, and not breathing. What should be your very first immediate action in resuscitation?

options.C: Administer intravenous antibiotics right away

question: What is the best way for a nursing team to share their successful hospital study with others?

options.A: Keeping the final report locked inside a private desk drawer

explanation: Good nursing knowledge is meant to be shared! Conferences and journals help spread great ideas so patient care improves everywhere.

question: What is the primary function of the gallbladder?

options.A: To manufacture digestive enzymes

question: A family's well water is muddy with visible dirt particles. What should they do first before treating it?

question: Why does a lower pH number mean higher acidity?

question: Why do busy hospital wards rely on a clear chain of command?

options.D: It eliminates all potential conflicts between doctors and nurses

explanation: Spot on! A clear chain of command simply means everyone knows who to run to for guidance and decisions when things get busy on the ward.

question: Which of the following is NOT a normal function or feature of the large intestine?

options.A: Housing beneficial bacteria that synthesize vitamin K

question: A nurse is planning care for an adult patient who presents with chronic pelvic pain and severe emotional distress related to FGM. What should be the first priority in her management?

question: Which of the following is an absolute contraindication for gastric lavage?

question: How do telehealth and home monitoring devices truly help patients living with chronic illnesses?

question: Which of the following is NOT a common challenge faced by nurses providing community care for special children in Nigeria?

question: What is the main job of a Nurse Principal Investigator?

question: A clinic is starting a digital triage system but keeps paper registers nearby just in case the network goes down. What is this strategy called?

question: A patient's pulse oximeter shows 82%, but they are talking and breathing easily. What should you do first?

question: A nurse implements strict handwashing and ensures a clean, well-ventilated ward to prevent infection outbreaks. Whose historical principles are being applied here?

options.A: Hippocrates

question: What is the primary purpose of developmental screening tools used by nurses?

question: A nurse organizes a community screening program to check blood sugar levels in adults over forty. Which level of prevention does this represent?

question: Which of these is a biological factor that affects emotional health?

question: Why does the pregnant body develop normal insulin resistance during later gestation?

question: Which type of measure tells us the final, ultimate impact of care on the patient's health?

question: Why is it unsafe to use ordinary adhesive tape to fix a frayed electrical cord on a medical device?

question: Which sign warns you that the uterus might soon rupture during prolonged, difficult labor?

question: How do combined oral contraceptive pills (COCPs) mainly prevent pregnancy?

question: What is the term for fake emails that try to trick hospital staff into giving up their passwords?

question: Which of these is a direct legal duty for a nurse administrator?

question: What is polypharmacy, a common concern in care home residents?

question: Which physical finding is a classic sign of severe protein deficiency?

question: What is the primary purpose of an Electronic Health Record (EHR)?

question: What is the main goal of a 'just culture' in healthcare?

question: What part do community elders usually play in keeping traditional food beliefs alive?

question: When does NEMA usually send out relief materials like food and shelter items?

question: What is a major feature of employer-sponsored health insurance?

question: How do traditional inheritance customs keep the strong preference for male children alive?

question: How do disaster preparedness drills and community workshops help with long-term recovery goals?

question: Why is receiving feedback from a tertiary center important for a primary care nurse?

question: How is the role of a nurse in assisted living different from a nurse in a busy hospital?

options.B: To rely completely on single-use plastics
options.C: To require buying advanced technology from abroad
options.D: To encourage using low-cost, locally available items

explanation: Correct! Sustainable care uses things people can easily find, afford, and fix right in their own neighborhoods without breaking the bank.

question: Near the end of life, what is the primary focus of palliative psychological care?

options.A: Finding a sudden cure for the advanced condition
options.B: Promoting comfort, dignity, and emotional peace
options.C: Preventing family members from visiting the patient
options.D: Encouraging aggressive life-extending surgeries

explanation: Palliative care centers entirely on quality of life, surrounding the patient with warmth, respect, and peace.

question: What is the main job of a hospital's infection control unit?

options.A: To reduce the risk of spreading infections within the facility
options.B: To handle the daily administrative duties of the pharmacy
options.C: To hire and train new doctors for surgical departments
options.D: To lower the overall cost of running hospital laboratories

explanation: Spot on! The primary focus of infection control is to protect both patients and staff by stopping harmful germs from spreading.

question: When we talk about the 'virulence' of a germ, what do we mean?

options.A: The ability of the organism to simply enter and multiply inside a human host
options.B: The total number of people who have been exposed to the microorganism
options.C: The speed at which the pathogen can travel through the open air
options.D: The severity of the disease and the likelihood of causing severe illness or death

explanation: Virulence is basically how fierce or damaging the germ is. A highly virulent germ packs a really heavy punch!

question: What popular model explains that errors happen when multiple system defenses fail all at once?

options.A: The SBAR communication chain
options.B: The Swiss cheese model
options.C: The root cause hierarchy
options.D: The Just Culture pyramid

explanation: You got it! Think of safety layers like slices of Swiss cheese. Accidents only happen when the holes in every single slice line up at the same time.

question: Which group acts as the most direct bridge between the home and the school?

options.A: Parent-Teacher Association
options.B: International donor agencies
options.C: Commercial transport unions
options.D: Federal Ministry of Finance

explanation: The PTA brings parents and teachers together directly to address the welfare and health needs of the students. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T6#GNS225_U4_T6_h2)

question: How should a nurse view a patient's relapse during long-term addiction recovery?

options.A: As definitive proof that the patient will never recover
options.B: As an indicator that the treatment plan needs adjustment
options.C: As a personal moral failure by the individual
options.D: As a minor event that requires no change in clinical care

explanation: Addiction is a chronic relapsing condition, meaning a return to use signals that support strategies or medications need re-evaluation. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T12#GNS125_U2_T12_h8)

question: Which rehab team member helps patients master everyday tasks like eating, bathing, and dressing?

options.A: Physiatrist
options.B: Physical therapist
options.C: Occupational therapist
options.D: Speech-language pathologist

explanation: Occupational therapists (OTs) are the masters of 'occupations'—meaning everyday living activities. They help patients get back to doing things for themselves!

question: Why must you always lock your computer screen when walking away from the nurses' station?

options.A: To prevent the central processing unit from overheating during idle times
options.B: To automatically save any unsaved nursing notes to the cloud
options.C: To save electrical power and extend the lifespan of the monitor display
options.D: To protect patient privacy and prevent unauthorized access to health records

explanation: Leaving a screen unlocked risks patient confidentiality. A quick lock keeps sensitive health records safe from prying eyes!

question: A nurse notices that a patient's skin is very dry and lacks normal turgor. Which physiological issue does this most likely suggest?

options.A: Dehydration and fluid volume deficit
options.B: Excessive vitamin D production
options.C: Normal localized blood pooling
options.D: High levels of subcutaneous fat

explanation: Poor skin turgor and dryness are classic clinical signs of fluid loss and dehydration. [learn more](GNS211_U2_T5#GNS211_U2_T5_h8)

question: Under the Abuja Declaration, what percentage of their annual budget should African governments put toward health?

options.A: Five percent of private sector corporate profits
options.B: Ten percent of all international donor funds received
options.C: Exactly 50 percent of the total Gross Domestic Product
options.D: At least 15 percent of the annual national budget

explanation: The famous Abuja Declaration set a benchmark of at least 15% for national health budgets. Great to keep in mind for your exams!

question: A nurse manager wants to present fall rates to bedside nurses to improve safety. How should she present it?

options.A: Emphasize the financial penalties the hospital faces from insurance
options.B: Present complex statistical regression models without explanation
options.C: Read the entire hospital policy manual out loud to the team
options.D: Focus on how shift routines and practical steps can prevent falls

explanation: Exactly! Bedside nurses love practical tips that fit into their daily ward routine and make patient care safer.

question: A mother is worried that routine immunizations will make her baby sick with a fever. What is the best way to reassure her?

options.A: Tell her that vaccines contain dangerous live disease organisms
options.B: Suggest she waits until the child starts school before vaccinating
options.C: Advise her to skip all future injections to keep the baby safe
options.D: Explain that mild fever is a normal sign the body is building immunity

explanation: You got it! A low-grade fever or soreness just means the baby's immune system is actively working out and building strong protection.

question: What does the letter 'B' stand for in the SBAR communication tool?

options.A: Bedside
options.B: Behavior
options.C: Background
options.D: Briefing

explanation: Spot on! 'B' stands for Background, giving the history and context that led up to the current issue.

question: What is the primary setting for a psychiatric home visit?

options.A: Inside a secure prison psychiatric ward
options.B: Inside a traditional healing spiritual center
options.C: Inside a busy outpatient clinic waiting room
options.D: Inside the client's private residence

explanation: Home visits specifically take place within the client's home environment to observe their daily life and functioning. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T6#GNS314_U4_T6_h1)

question: What is the most important piece of advice to give a patient who has recovered from serum sickness before they leave the hospital?

options.A: Demonstrate how to measure blood pressure at home twice daily
options.B: Encourage the patient to eat a high-protein diet to rebuild lost muscle
options.C: Instruct the patient to exercise their joints vigorously every single morning
options.D: Teach the patient to permanently avoid the specific triggering drug

explanation: Prevention is key! They must avoid that specific drug forever, because taking it again can cause an even faster and worse reaction.

question: Why do local rescue teams worry so much about crowd control at a disaster site?

options.A: Crowds prevent media houses from broadcasting live updates
options.B: Uncontrolled crowds often steal heavy rescue machinery
options.C: Large crowds block access roads, delay ambulances, and endanger more lives
options.D: Onlookers are required by law to assist professional paramedics

explanation: You got it! Too many curious onlookers block the roads, stopping ambulances from getting through and putting even more people in danger.

question: Why did ancient people use fermentation for baking and brewing long before anyone discovered microbes?

options.A: They followed strict written instructions left by early microbiologists
options.B: They observed the practical results of microbial action without knowing the cause
options.C: They accidentally stumbled upon chemicals that preserved food permanently
options.D: They possessed advanced microscopes made of polished river stones

explanation: Ancient folks didn't know about germs yet, but they knew bread dough rises and palm wine ferments through trial and observation! Great job.

question: Why did military nursing groups become so important during the Crusades?

options.A: To translate ancient Greek philosophy texts
options.B: To provide organized shelter and treat wounded soldiers
options.C: To manufacture advanced gunpowder and tactical weapons
options.D: To govern newly conquered political territories

explanation: During the Crusades, special nursing groups were needed to set up safe resting places and care for fighters and travelers who got hurt.

question: On a scatter diagram, what does a single dot represent?

options.A: The total average of all patients in the study
options.B: The error rate of the measuring instrument
options.C: The difference between two hospital wards
options.D: One subject's values for both variables combined

explanation: Each dot is like a snapshot for one individual participant, showing both of their measurements meeting at a point.

question: How does the Vector Space Model determine which documents are the best match?

options.A: By checking how many times the patient's name appears in the text
options.B: By calculating the mathematical overlap between search terms and document themes
options.C: By asking the original author of the paper to vote on its usefulness
options.D: By selecting files created on the same calendar day

explanation: The vector space model measures the closeness of keywords and document concepts in a mathematical space to rank results. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T8#GNS113_U2_T8_h3)

question: What goes wrong if you crush an extended-release capsule before giving it to a patient?

options.A: The medication will take twice as long to work
options.B: The entire dose is released at once, risking toxicity
options.C: The patient will experience no therapeutic effect
options.D: The active ingredients are completely destroyed

explanation: Crushing destroys the special timed-release design. Instead of a steady, safe trickle of medicine over hours, the patient gets a dangerous flood all at once!

question: Which of these is a great example of working with another sector to stop the spread of infections like cholera?

options.A: Hospital pharmacists reviewing drug expiration dates in the dispensary
options.B: Doctors prescribing antibiotics in a private clinic setting
options.C: A head nurse holding a closed meeting with junior nursing students
options.D: Working with public works to ensure clean water supply to prevent cholera

explanation: Spot on! Teaming up with public works to fix water infrastructure stops waterborne diseases right at the source.

question: A patient with a severe absorption problem eats enough food but still loses weight. Why does this happen?

options.A: The damaged intestinal lining cannot properly transfer digested nutrients into the body
options.B: The liver stops producing bile needed to break down water
options.C: The stomach blocks food from entering the small intestine entirely
options.D: The large intestine absorbs all nutrients before they reach the bloodstream

explanation: Even though food is eaten, a damaged absorptive surface means the nutrients just pass through without getting into circulation. You're doing great!

question: Which stage of digestion gets triggered simply by the sight, smell, or even thought of delicious food?

options.A: Absorptive phase
options.B: Intestinal phase
options.C: Cephalic phase
options.D: Gastric phase

explanation: Ever start salivating just thinking about jollof rice? That's the cephalic phase at work—your brain priming your digestive system before food even touches your lips!

question: How should a nurse manager respond when a staff member makes an honest, unintentional calculation slip?

options.A: Ignore the incident since no patient was actually harmed
options.B: Immediately terminate the nurse to set an example for others
options.C: Provide comfort and look at ways to improve the system
options.D: Report the nurse to the police for criminal negligence

explanation: Spot on! In a Just Culture, honest human error calls for support and system fixes, not unfair punishment. Learning is a journey!

question: Which organ is the main player in the 'first-pass effect' for oral drugs?

options.A: The kidneys
options.B: The pancreas
options.C: The liver
options.D: The stomach

explanation: You guessed it—the liver! Blood from the gut goes straight to the liver via the portal vein, where enzymes process and break down a portion of the drug before it hits the rest of the body.

question: Which health indicator typically gets better as a country's GNP goes up?

options.A: Incidence of waterborne diseases
options.B: Infant mortality rate
options.C: General population morbidity
options.D: Rate of chronic malnutrition

explanation: As a nation grows wealthier, it can afford better maternal and child healthcare, which means fewer babies dying in infancy. Great health systems start with strong economies!

question: What does creating a healthcare policy actually involve?

options.A: Cleaning hospital wards after a surgical procedure
options.B: Diagnosing rare tropical diseases in a laboratory
options.C: Administering daily medication to individual patients
options.D: Creating guidelines and rules that govern health delivery

explanation: Policies are simply the official rules and guidelines that shape how healthcare systems are run.

question: Giving routine childhood vaccinations to prevent measles is an example of which level of prevention?

options.A: Quaternary prevention
options.B: Primary prevention
options.C: Tertiary prevention
options.D: Secondary prevention

explanation: Primary prevention stops a disease before it happens by protecting healthy individuals through methods like vaccination. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T2#GNS313_U2_T2_h2)

question: Whose responsibility is it to ensure visitors follow isolation rules in a patient's room?

options.A: The nurse caring for the patient
options.B: The patient staying in the room
options.C: The hospital security guards
options.D: The dietary staff delivering meals

explanation: Nurses are responsible for educating visitors and making sure everyone entering the isolation room adheres to safety protocols. [learn more](GST114_U2_T17#GST114_U2_T17_h8)

question: For how long is exclusive breastfeeding recommended for a healthy baby?

options.A: Until the first birthday
options.B: First three months of life
options.C: First six months of life
options.D: Until the baby starts walking

explanation: Spot on! Exclusive breastfeeding for the first six months gives babies the absolute best nutrition and shields them against common childhood sicknesses.

question: What is the primary purpose of community herd immunity?

options.A: To guarantee lifelong immunity against common viral colds
options.B: To protect vulnerable individuals who cannot safely receive vaccines
options.C: To ensure pharmaceutical companies produce enough medication
options.D: To completely eliminate the need for hand hygiene in hospitals

explanation: When most of the community is vaccinated, germs struggle to spread, shielding babies or sick patients who cannot get immunized. [learn more](GST114_U1_T3#GST114_U1_T3_h6)

question: What is the main job of a 'hard stop' in a computer health system?

options.A: To prevent entry of illogical data or dangerous orders
options.B: To automatically log out nurses who take a meal break
options.C: To block patients from viewing their own lab results
options.D: To delete duplicate patient charts at the end of the day

explanation: A hard stop forces you to fix unusual values or double-check safety alerts before you can move forward.

question: Why is organizing clinical data like a story so helpful?

options.A: It hides negative statistics so the hospital looks better
options.B: It guarantees that hospital administration will approve more funding
options.C: It legally protects the nursing staff from medical malpractice claims
options.D: It guides the audience logically and prevents cognitive overload

explanation: Great job! A clear beginning, middle, and end helps everyone digest heavy facts without feeling overwhelmed.

question: Which behavior in a just culture is characterized by an inadvertent slip or unintentional mistake?

options.A: Criminal negligence
options.B: Human error
options.C: Reckless behavior
options.D: At-risk behavior

explanation: Human error represents an accidental lapse or slip where the worker did not intend to cause a problem. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T9#GNS312_U5_T9_h5)

question: Why must a nurse evaluate the road conditions and distance to the hospital for a home birth?

options.A: To calculate how much fuel the nurse's car will burn
options.B: To find the cheapest taxi fare for the family
options.C: To decide if the baby will be born during the day or night
options.D: To plan a safe and fast emergency transfer if complications happen

explanation: If labor goes wrong, bad roads or long distances can delay life-saving hospital care. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T8#GNS225_U3_T8_h6)

question: Which of these sits at the very top of the healthcare policy framework?

options.A: Ward shift handover notes
options.B: National laws and legislative acts
options.C: Hospital-wide administrative bylaws
options.D: Individual departmental protocols

explanation: Always remember: external national laws and acts overrule every internal hospital rule and departmental guideline.

question: Which of these is NOT a good way to work with traditional healers in a local community?

options.A: Educating them on the danger of delayed hospital treatment
options.B: Insulting their practices publicly to show modern medical superiority
options.C: Inviting them to dialogue meetings to discuss patient safety
options.D: Finding ways to build respectful referral links with them

explanation: Spot on! Publicly shaming traditional practitioners only creates bitterness and drives patients away from getting the formal care they need.

question: A rural health post keeps running out of basic drugs and has no steady electricity. Which part of health economics is this?

options.A: The age distribution of the community
options.B: The supply of health services
options.C: The cultural beliefs of the patients
options.D: The overall consumer demand curve

explanation: You nailed it! Things like drugs, equipment, and steady power are vital parts of healthcare *supply*. When they are missing, the clinic's ability to provide care drops.

question: Which imaging test uses a special dye to check the urethra for tears before putting in a catheter?

options.A: Intravenous pyelogram scan
options.B: Retrograde urethrogram
options.C: Plain abdominal X-ray
options.D: Renal duplex ultrasound

explanation: A retrograde urethrogram involves gently putting contrast dye into the urethral opening to take a picture and ensure there are no tears before inserting any tubes.
